Criterion: Verify that a misserviced shock strut safely supports all weapons loading, fueling and defueling, does not compromise takeoff and landings, and does not result in ground resonance. Standard: Misserviced shock struts do not adversely affect dynamic energy absorption or adversely affect air vehicle structure. Sudden and adverse movements of the strut do not occur during weapons, fuel, and other loading events. During takeoff, landing and taxi events no damage occurs to the landing gear system or to the air vehicle structure as long as the pressure within the strut stays within the misservicing range. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analyses, tests, inspections and demonstrations. Shock strut energy analysis verifies that air vehicle loads are not exceeded for misserviced shock strut pressures and at all air vehicle operational weights. Ground demonstrations and inspection verify that the landing gear system maintains satisfactory attitudes during ground operations such as fueling, weapons loading, etc. Component testing verifies that the landing gear system performs as designed when misserviced within the specified range of pressures. Flight and ground air vehicle testing validate the analysis and verify the operational suitability of the shock strut. References: AFGS-87139: 3.2.1.3 Clearances MIL-T-6053 (Inactive for New Design) MIL-L-8552 14 CFR 13.1-13.2.4, 23.1501, 23.1529, 25.1501, 25.1503-25.1533, 25.1529, 25.1541, 25.1543, 25.1557, 25.1563

Standard: No damage or functional impairment (e.g., dynamic energy absorption) occurs to the landing gear system or air vehicle structure during taxi, takeoff, and landing events with the mis-servicing levels listed in TABLE V. TABLE V. Shock strut mis-servicing allowances. Air Vehicle Gas Pressure Oil Volume Tire Pressure Fixed-wing ±10% 100% fluid level minus 0.5-inch of oleo stroke Fixed-wing Aircraft Carrier ±15% ±15% ±20% Rotary-wing ±20% ±10% ±20% Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Conduct dynamic analysis of the shock absorber to verify damping characteristics and establish landing limit load cases (e.g., level, tail down, and multivariate) under mis-serviced conditions. Analysis identifies worst-case loads. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Conduct full scale drop testing of nose and main landing gear assemblies with wheels spun up in a reverse direction to reflect landing speed at worst-case load conditions to verify metering and damping effectiveness, loads (e.g., spin up and spring back), clearances, strut frictions, stroking, and bottoming characteristics of the landing shock absorbers at mis-serviced conditions. The landing gear assembly includes shock absorbers, wheels, tires, brakes, actuators, locks and other structural members as used on the air vehicle. Conduct testing as follows: a. For USAF air vehicles, drop testing of mis-servicing cases are conducted IAW SAE AS6053A, Miscellaneous Landing Tests paragraph. b. For USN air vehicles, drop testing cases can be defined based on the nominal and worst-case landing conditions developed from Analysis MoC (1). Resulting loads correlate with analytical predictions. c. For rotary-wing landing gear is at a limit sink speed of 12 ft/s in combination with 1g rotor lift and address landing cases including all combinations of the following: all horizontal speeds from 30 kts rearward to the best forward speed for minimum rate of descent in autorotation, air vehicle pitch attitudes (ranging from 15-degrees nose down to 15-degrees tail down), combinations of sinking speed and roll angle lying on and within the envelopes, and brakes locked and unlocked operations for VLs.
